newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila vows "complete safety" for APEC leaders.
newsitem.headline: Manila vows "complete safety" for APEC leaders.

text.p: President Fidel Ramos said on Sunday he could assure the "complete safety" of the leaders of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum at their summit in the Philippines this month.

Leaders of leftist groups planning to hold an anti-APEC meeting to coincide with the November 25 summit have accused the army and police of harassing and putting their supporters under surveillance on suspicion they would try to disrupt the summit.
They also accused the government of demolishing the shanties of thousands of squatters in Manila to hide widespread poverty.
"We can assure all APEC delegations...at the level of the businessmen all way up to the leaders, complete safety (and) comfort," Ramos said.
Ramos spoke to reporters at Subic Bay freeport, the summit's venue and former site of a major U.S. Navy base, to inaugurate the passenger terminal building of its international airport.
Security officials have said they are not aware of specific threats to any APEC leader but are deploying several police battalions around the sites of APEC meetings as a precaution.

The government has banned Nobel peace laureate and East Timorese resistance leader Jose Ramos-Horta from entering the country to attend an international meeting of non-governmental organisations (NGO) coinciding with the APEC meetings.
Manila says Ramos-Horta's presence at the NGO meeting, where he wanted to speak on the East Timor issue, might be "disruptive."
Indonesian President Suharto, whose government annexed East Timor in 1976 in a move never recognised by the United Nations, is among the leaders attending the APEC summit.
